title: Higher-Winding Fractionalization
authors: Kishore Iyer, Christophe Mora, Daniele Guerci
abstract: Higher-winding skyrmion textures can generate emergent magnetic fields with multiple flux quanta per unit cell. This opens an intriguing route toward fractionalization, allowing fractionalized quantum anomalous Hall states to arise even at integer filling of the microscopic unit cell. We show that, in this setting, increasing lattice-scale inhomogeneity of the emergent magnetic field drives a Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) transition between a fractionalized liquid and a crystalline dielectric state. This transition carries a topological signature: under flux insertion, the many-body polarization defines a quantized winding number that is nonzero in the fractionalized phase and vanishes in the dielectric crystal.
summary: This work explores how higher-winding skyrmion textures induce fractionalization in electronic systems, leading to Fractional Chern Insulator (FCI) states. The key finding is that increasing spatial inhomogeneity in the emergent magnetic field drives a BKT transition from the highly correlated FCI liquid phase into a stable crystalline dielectric phase. The analysis uses advanced techniques like Coulomb gas mapping and RG theory to pinpoint this topological transition.
main_problem: The paper investigates fractionalization in topological phases using higher-winding skyrmion textures, allowing for fractionalized quantum anomalous Hall states even at integer filling.
main_result: Increasing the inhomogeneity of the emergent magnetic field drives a Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless (BKT) transition from a fractionalized liquid (FCI) to a crystalline dielectric state, characterized by the vanishing of a quantized winding number.
method: The analysis involves mapping the many-body ground state to a 2D Coulomb gas model and employing Renormalization Group (RG) techniques to characterize the phase transition.
model_or_system: The system models interacting electrons coupled to higher-winding skyrmion textures ($Q>1$), described by an effective Hamiltonian in the Aharonov–Casher limit. The study focuses on the competition between the FCI liquid and a crystalline dielectric state.
key_observables: Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}$), dielectric constant ($\epsilon^{-1}$), connected static structure factor ($S(q)$), and the many-body polarization winding number.
important_parameters:
Higher winding number ($Q$), lattice inhomogeneity parameter ($K$), and filling fraction ($
u$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-exchange limit ($Jm^*a^2/\hbar^2 \gg 1$) and mapping the system to a Coulomb gas model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the low-energy manifold for $Q=3$, the evolution of the structure factor $S(q)$ across the transition, and the pair correlation function $g(r)$ showing liquid-to-crystalline changes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the model using skyrmion textures, deriving the effective Hamiltonian, analyzing the topological properties via the Coulomb gas mapping, and finally characterizing the BKT transition using RG flow and correlation functions.
why_interesting: The study provides a concrete, tunable platform (skyrmion texture) to realize and study fundamental many-body phenomena like fractionalization and topological phase transitions, which are key areas of interest in AMO physics and condensed matter theory.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Higher-winding skyrmion model bands and fractionalization at filling ν = 1. The low-energy manifold for Jm∗a2/(π2ℏ2) = 100 consists of Q = 3 flat bands with total Chern number |Ctot| = 1, which become degenerate in the infinite-J limit. Many-body spectrum vs. center of mass momentum q, from ED on a 3×3 torus for electrons at filling ν = 1, using the three lowest energy bands with V1 interaction at K = 0.4. The ground state is threefold degenerate.

FIG. 2. Topological response and perfect screening of the ideal FCI. (a) Many-body positions X1 (blue) and X2 (orange) under flux insertion ϕ2. (b) Connected static structure factor S(q) along qx in unit of ℓ2 = AUC/(2πQ), where the solid parabola shows the long-wavelength behavior. Plots are for N = 192 electrons at K = 0.4.

FIG. 3. Evolution of the many-body spectrum and of the long wavelength behavior of S(q). (a) Spectrum versus magnetic-field modulation K for V1 interactions at ν = 1 and emergent flux 3h/e per unit cell. The calculation retains the three lowest bands on a 3 × 3 cluster. (b) 4πS(q)/q2 at q = ∆k, with ∆k momentum resolution, as a function of K for N = 243 electrons.

FIG. 4. Many-body polarization and center of mass fluctuations. Panel (a): Top and bottom panels show the evolution of X1/2 and ζ1,2, respectively, as a function of ϕ2 ∈[0, 6π) upon increasing K. Panel (b): Evolution of the twist averaged center- of-mass fluctuations ∆R1,2. The vertical dashed line denotes the topological transition. Plots are for N = 243 electrons.
